claims.text: A method combining ab initio molecular dynamics with machine-learning potentials is proposed.

Incorporating machine-learning potentials into ab initio molecular-dynamics simulations will substantially reduce the computational cost of obtaining fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties for high-entropy systems.
The proposed method will preserve the accuracy of solid-state free energies, fluid-state free energies, and relevant entropy terms.
The proposed method is intended to apply from 1000 K to 3000 K.
The proposed method is intended to apply to high-entropy systems containing no more than five components.
The machine-learning potentials will be trained on ab initio data.
Machine-learning potentials can learn the complex interatomic interactions in high-entropy systems.
Learning these interatomic interactions will reduce computational cost while maintaining accuracy.
The proposed method will reduce computational cost by at least 50% relative to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows.
The proposed method will increase throughput by 20% relative to TOR-TILD.
The proposed method will achieve at least 95% accuracy for solid and fluid free energies and relevant entropy terms relative to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows.
Applications above 3000 K may require additional training data or adjustments to the machine-learning potentials.
Applications to systems containing more than five components may require additional training data or adjustments to the machine-learning potentials.
The accuracy of the machine-learning potentials may depend on the quality and quantity of the training data.
Limited transferability to new systems or conditions may reduce the accuracy of the machine-learning potentials.
The benchmark will compare computational cost, solid and fluid free energies, and relevant entropy terms against explicit ab initio molecular dynamics and TOR-TILD.
The hypothesis is declared falsified if cost reduction is below 30% or accuracy is below 90% relative to explicit ab initio molecular dynamics.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome requires at least 50% cost reduction and at least 95% accuracy, but the falsification rule permits 30–49% cost reduction and 90–94% accuracy without falsifying the hypothesis. Thus, failure to achieve the stated prediction is not itself decisive under the proposed rule.
